President Emmanuel Macron is due to lead the main memorial ceremony later on Tuesday, while a minute's silence will be observed before France's World Cup semi-final against Spain.

Ces Méga-feux sont-ils une nouvelle norme ?

france24fr.title: Zimbabwe : 80 000 rapatriés après les violences en Afrique du Sud
france24fr.description: Près de 80 000 Zimbabwéens ont regagné leur pays après les violences xénophobes en Afrique du Sud. La majorité est revenue par ses propres moyens, malgré un dispositif de rapatriement mis en place par les autorités. De retour chez eux, ils racontent les épreuves et les traumatismes qu'ils ont vécus.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l’aventure s’arrête pour les Bleus
france24fr.description: Hors course pour le gain du titre, l'équipe de France n'en a pourtant pas fini avec la Coupe du monde puisqu'elle disputera le match pour la troisième place, samedi à Miami, contre le perdant d'Angleterre-Argentine, une partie à la portée purement symbolique mais qui ne sera pas dénuée d'enjeux pour les Bleus.

france24fr.title: France : le Parlement vote une dernière fois pour la création d'un droit à l'aide à mourir
france24fr.description: Un long processus qui s'achève : les députés devraient approuver définitivement mercredi, lors d'un quatrième et ultime vote, la loi créant un "droit à l'aide à mourir", réforme sociétale majeure du second quinquennat d'Emmanuel Macron.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Bleus éliminés par la Roja
france24fr.description: La France et son attaque jusqu'alors étincelante ont échoué dans leur quête d'une troisième finale de Coupe du monde. Les hommes de Didier Deschamps ayant été totalement muselés par une équipe d'Espagne parfaitement organisée. La deuxième demi-finale de ce Mondial oppose donc à Atlanta l'Argentine à l'Angleterre ce mercredi.

france24fr.title: Forêt de Fontainebleau : les pompiers cherchent à contenir les reprises de feu
france24fr.description: Un homme suspecté d'avoir voulu provoquer un incendie a été interpellé mardi soir sur un parking près de la forêt de Fontainebleau et placé en garde à vue, tandis que quelque 800 pompiers tentaient toujours de circonscrire les reprises de feu mercredi matin dans le massif.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : les soignants dénoncent leurs conditions de travail
france24fr.description: L’ampleur de l'épidémie actuelle d'Ebola pourrait représenter deux à quatre fois les estimations officielles annonces faites par l'OMS. Le dernier bilan officiel des autorités congolaises publié mardi fait état de 719 morts et 1963 personnes contaminées. Dans l’Ituri, des soignants ont protesté ce mardi pour dénoncer leurs conditions de travail.

france24fr.title: Haïti dans les griffes des gangs : la crise humanitaire s'éternise
france24fr.description: En Haïti, la capitale et certaines provinces restent en état de siège et la population est toujours otage des gangs armés. Une situation de chaos qui aggrave la crise humanitaire. La distribution de l'aide humanitaire est un défi quotidien : l'accès à Port-au-Prince par la route est impossible et l'aéroport n'opère que périodiquement. En dépit de ces obstacles, les organisations humanitaires continuent d'aider la population. Roméo Langlois et Catherine Norris Trent se sont rendus sur place.

france24fr.title: Incendies à Fontainebleau : une forêt marquée par le passage des flammes
france24fr.description: Des incendies ont ravagé environ 2 050 hectares de la célèbre forêt de Fontainebleau, au sud-est de Paris, depuis qu'ils se sont déclarés dimanche 12 juillet. Les feux ont contraint environ 1 000 personnes à évacuer. Quelque 800 pompiers étaient encore à pied d'œuvre mercredi matin pour contenir les reprises de feu, qui ont été fixés la veille après 48 heures de lutte intense. Les explications de Julie Dungelhoeff, notre envoyée spéciale à Achères-la-Forêt

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Argentine sait souffrir et gagner ses matches dans le dernier quart d'heure
france24fr.description: Avec neuf buts marqués après la 80e minute, l’Argentine se montre comme une spécialiste des qualifications au bout de l’effort. Elle a appris à souffrir au fil de la compétition et comptera une nouvelle fois sur le génie de Messi ou l'inspiration tardive de ses attaquants pour battre l'Angleterre en demi-finale du Mondial, mercredi.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ukraine : Ursula von der Leyen annonce un accord entre l'UE et Kiev sur la production de drones
États-Unis : les contrôles routiers de l'ICE suspendus après deux décès
france24fr.description: L’administration Trump a ordonné la suspension de la plupart des contrôles routiers menés par l'ICE, alors que deux hommes ont été abattus par des agents en moins d’une semaine.

france24fr.title: Fontainebleau : les reprises de feu compliquent la tâche des pompiers, nouvelle garde à vue
france24fr.description: Un homme de 46 ans suspecté d'avoir voulu provoquer un incendie a été interpellé mardi soir  près de la forêt de Fontainebleau et placé en garde à vue selon une source policière. De nombreux journaux froissés et un briquet ont été retrouvés dans son véhicule. Mercredi matin, quelque 800 pompiers tentaient toujours de contenir les reprises de feu dans le massif.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Moyen-Orient en direct : l'armée américaine annonce une nouvelle "vague de frappes" en Iran
Mondial 2026 : l'autopsie tactique de la défaite des Bleus en demi-finale
france24fr.description: L'élimination de la France mardi en demi-finales du Mondial face à l'Espagne laisse un goût d'inachevé après les promesses suscitées par le jeu flamboyant déployé tout au long de la compétition. Pour certains, les remplacements de Didier Deschamps durant la rencontre ont considérablement pesé sur cette défaite.

france24fr.title: Mali-Algérie : les deux pays amorcent un rapprochement après une longue crise
france24fr.description: Après plus d’un an de tensions, Bamako et Alger amorcent un retour au dialogue. Les deux pays ont annoncé vendredi la réouverture de leurs espaces aériens respectifs et le retour de leurs ambassadeurs, marquant une première étape vers la normalisation de leurs relations. les précisions de Mohamed Amara, sociologue.

france24fr.title: Chassés d’Afrique du Sud, des Zimbabwéens racontent leur calvaire
france24fr.description: Après des semaines de calvaire, près de 80 000 Zimbabwéens ont regagné leur pays depuis la fin du mois… avec, pour beaucoup, des traumatismes liés aux violences xénophobes en Afrique du Sud. Ils racontent les épreuves qu’ils ont traversées.

zeit.description: Bei der Bundeswehr gingen im Juni mehr als 40.000 Bewerbungen ein und damit fast ein Viertel mehr als noch vor einem Jahr. Auch die Zahl der Neueinstellungen stieg.

zeit.title: Joseph Weiler: »Die Fifa ist eine hässliche Organisation«
zeit.description: Der Versuch, die Fifa zu reformieren, ist gescheitert. Joseph Weiler weiß das, er hat es im Auftrag der Fifa versucht. Doch das heisst nicht, dass Fußball am Ende ist.

nzz.title: Verbot von Wegwerf-E-Zigaretten: Die Kantone dürfen den Bund übersteuern

nzz.title: Juden, Amerikaner und finstere Machenschaften – im Nahen Osten sind immer die anderen schuld
nzz.description: Die Fifa wird von Zionisten gesteuert, und Lionel Messi ist in Wahrheit ein Jude: In der arabischen Welt stossen Verschwörungstheorien auch während der Fussball-WM auf grossen Widerhall.

nzz.title: Krisenstimmung in Peking: Chinas Wirtschaft verliert deutlich an Dynamik
nzz.description: Im zweiten Quartal fiel das Wachstum auf den tiefsten Stand seit mehr als drei Jahren. Nur einen Lichtblick gibt es: den Exportsektor.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Vier Tote, darunter ein sechsjähriges Mädchen, nach israelischem Luftangriff
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Russland-Angriff auf Odessa fordert drei Tote – Schwarzmeer-Konflikt spitzt sich zu
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Spritpreise steigen nach Ende des Tankrabatts deutlich – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.description: 3 Gastgeber, 48 Teilnehmer: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

observador.title: Banco Mundial quer melhorias nos transportes em Cabo Verde
observador.description: Representante do Banco Mundial no arquipélago pede "sistema de transportes interilhas fiável e acessível" para transformar a recuperação impulsionada pelo turismo.

observador.title: 108 faturas e 13 empresas: as contas das obras de Luís Neves
observador.description: MAI forneceu ao Observador lista detalhada das 108 faturas de 13 empresas nas obras em São Teotónio. Comprovativos de pagamento ainda não foram apresentados.

observador.title: Montenegro diz que Governo vai continuar "a arriscar"
observador.description: No 1.º Encontro Ciência e Inovação 2026, o primeiro-ministro destacou a importância de Portugal inovar e "perder o medo de falhar", sem mencionar diretamente a situação da correção digital dos exames.

observador.title: Bote baleeiro vai ser candidato a património da UNESCO
observador.description: Está em consulta pública a inscrição do Bote Baleeiro Açoriano no Inventário Nacional do Património Cultural Imaterial. Após a inscrição tem a intenção de se a património da UNESCO.

observador.title: Renováveis: mias de mil milhões em contribuições fiscais
observador.description: Associação indica que Portugal aplica carga fiscal "sem paralelo" na Europa. Setor está longe de beneficiar de um regime fiscal privilegiado. Renováveis geram poupança anual de 636 euros por agregado.

observador.description: Autarquia diz que implementação do programa "não assegura a adequada proteção do território e dos seus valores naturais, sociais e económicos". Insuficiências técnicas e territoriais continuam.

observador.title: A inflamação no papel de protagonista
observador.description: José Raposo troca o palco pelo laboratório e conversa com o cientista do GIMM, Miguel Soares, para perceber como a inflamação protege o organismo, mas também pode tornar-se causa de doenças graves.

observador.title: Mulher morre em incêndio em habitação nos Olivais em Lisboa
observador.description: Mulher de 82 anos morreu na sua habitação na sequência de um incêndio na freguesia dos Olivais, em Lisboa. Ainda são desconhecidas as causas do fogo.

observador.title: Madeira testa drones para transporte de bananas
observador.description: Iniciativa insere-se na aposta do executivo regional na "inovação e modernização do setor primário". Contribui para o escoamento da produção e preserva a "paisagem agrícola madeirense".

observador.title: GEOTA considera barragem de Girabolhos "erro estratégico"
observador.description: GEOTA afirma que a construção da barragem de Girabolhos é ilegal porque não foi realizada a avaliação de impacte ambiental. As cheias da região não resultam da falta de barragem mas da má gestão.

observador.title: Conferência de Líderes condena vídeo de Ventura
observador.description: Os líderes parlamentares condenaram o vídeo gravado por André Ventura a indiciar que ninguém estava no Parlamento a trabalhar. Pedro Pinto crítica postura de Aguiar-Branco.

observador.title: Juan Roig e Ana Botín no mundial e no "live" de youtuber
observador.description: Líderes empresariais espanhóis pediram a streamer ​​​​para tirar uma fotografia. Explicaram que Mercadona “é como um Walmart espanhol” e o Banco Santander “é como o JP Morgan da Europa”.

observador.title: Luís Neves está num pântano ou simplesmente num tanque?
observador.description: No "Realpolitik", Sérgio Sousa Pinto e Miguel Pinheiro falam sobre a polémica com Luís Neves, sobre o estado do governo e sobre o combate entre Nigel Farage e o Conde Cara de Caixote do Lixo.

observador.title: Será a Argentina a mesma que conhecíamos?
observador.description: O encontro Argentina x Inglaterra promete ser um “grande espetáculo de futebol”. Há dúvidas de que a equipa sul americana mantenha a performance do Mundial anterior frente a uma Inglaterra melhorada.

observador.title: PS questiona UE sobre detenção de Domingos Simões Pereira
observador.description: Socialistas questionam Kaja Kallas sobre detenção do líder guineense, com base em "acusações forjadas" sobre alegada tentativa de golpe de Estado. Guiné-Bissau prepara referendo constitucional.

observador.title: AR. Debate sobre os exames marcado para sexta
observador.description: A Conferência de Líderes parlamentares convocou um debate de urgência sobre os exames para sexta-feira, depois do Estado da Nação. PCP diz que Aguiar Branco e a AD foram contra.

observador.title: Milagre do Hudson. Piloto Sully diagnosticado com Alzheimer
observador.description: Antigo piloto promete "falar abertamente" sobre a doença e apela à mesma coragem que mostrou ao salvar 155 vidas no rio Hudson, quando amarou de emergência o avião. Alzheimer está no "estado inicial".

spiegel.title: Markus Beierle ist tot: Ex-Bundesligastürmer von Eintracht Frankfurt mit 54 Jahren gestorben
spiegel.description: Gleich zweimal stieg er mit Eintracht Frankfurt in die Bundesliga auf, in der er mehr als 130 Spiele bestritt. Jetzt ist Markus Beierle im Alter von 54 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: KTF-Kürzungen: Antworten auf die wichtigsten Fragen
spiegel.description: Der Finanzminister braucht Geld – und holt es sich auch im Klima- und Transformationsfonds. Die Entscheidung beruht auf einer gewagten Begründung. Wen die Kürzungen treffen und wie es um bereits zugesagte Förderungen steht.

spiegel.title: Dresden: Mann zielt mit Waffe auf Supermarktbesucher und ruft islamischen Spruch
spiegel.description: Schock für die Besucher und Besucherinnen eines Dresdner Supermarkts: Ein Mann zielt am Mittwochmorgen mit einer Waffe wahllos auf Anwesende. Die Polizei rückt an, dann fallen Schüsse.

spiegel.title: »Ich-AGs« und falsche Harmoniesucht – die echten Gründe für das deutsche WM-Debakel
spiegel.description: Fahrradtour, Kakerlaken oder Frauenbesuche: Über das Scheitern der DFB-Elf gibt es wilde Spekulationen. Eine SPIEGEL-Rekonstruktion zeigt, wie wenig davon zutrifft. Und was wirklich im Team geschah.

spiegel.title: JIM-Plus-Studie: Jugendliche erleben Social Media als Drahtseilakt
spiegel.description: Intensiver Austausch und schnelle Informationen – aber auch Hass, Mobbing, Fake News und drastische Bilder: Für Jugendliche ist Social Media einer Studie zufolge eine ständige Achterbahnfahrt.

spiegel.title: Bayreuth: TV-Koch Alexander Herrmann trickste für Trinkgeld beim Koffertragen
spiegel.description: Als Jugendlicher arbeitete TV-Koch Alexander Herrmann während der Bayreuther Festspiele als Kofferträger. Dabei gab es oft großzügige Trinkgelder. Wieso, verrät Herrmann nun in einem Interview.

spiegel.title: AfD-Veranstaltung in Dessau: Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt nach Auftritt von Uwe Steimle
spiegel.description: Ein Attentäter für Friedrich Merz und Angela Merkel »an die Wand stellen«: Auf einer AfD-Veranstaltung erging sich Kabarettist Uwe Steimle in Gewaltfantasien. Das hat nun Folgen.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Die Messi-Verschwörung vor dem Halbfinale gegen England
spiegel.description: Die ausgebliebene Rote Karte. Strittige Schiedsrichterentscheidungen. Ungeahndete Fouls. Viele Fans (und auch einige Trainer) stellen sich die Frage, ob Lionel Messi und Argentinien bei der WM bevorzugt werden.

spiegel.title: Griechenland: So rüstet Athen sich gegen die extreme Hitze
spiegel.description: Überwachung per Drohnen, Klimaanlagen für die Ärmsten und 13.000 neue Bäume: Der Athener Bürgermeister Haris Doukas will die heißeste Hauptstadt Europas für die Zukunft rüsten. Welche Fehler anderer Metropolen er dabei vermeiden will.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Schwere Unwetter sorgen für Verletzte und heftige Schäden in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Und wieder Gewitter, Hagel, Starkregen: In Bayern, Baden-Württemberg und Thüringen gab es schwere Schäden durch Unwetter, mehrere Menschen wurden verletzt. Die Gefahr ist noch nicht überall gebannt.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Industrie verliert 177.000 Arbeitsplätze in einem Jahr
spiegel.description: Die schwache Konjunktur belastet den Arbeitsmarkt schwer. Insbesondere die deutsche Industrie trifft es hart. 2025 gingen im verarbeitenden Gewerbe 177.000 Arbeitsplätze verloren.

spiegel.title: AfD-Verbot in Thüringen? Hape Kerkeling soll bei Anhörung sprechen
spiegel.description: Sollten einzelne AfD-Landesverbände verboten werden? Darüber gab es in der Politik zuletzt eine Debatte, nun soll diese Frage auch im Landtag in Erfurt erörtert werden. Auf der Rednerliste: Entertainer Hape Kerkeling.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Phil Collins: Noel Gallagher hält mich nicht wirklich für den Antichristen
spiegel.description: Oasis-Songwriter Noel Gallagher hat häufig über Genesis-Frontmann Phil Collins gelästert. Nun könnten sich die beiden bei einer Preisverleihung begegnen. Collins glaubt zu wissen, welcher Song Gallagher getriggert hat.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Was vom Auftritt des Kanzlers auf der Sommerpressekonferenz bleibt – drei Erkenntnisse
spiegel.description: Eigenlob, ein bisschen Selbstkritik und direkte Worte an Wähler der AfD: Kanzler Friedrich Merz hat sich 90 Minuten lang Fragen der Hauptstadtjournalisten gestellt. Lesen Sie hier die Liveanalyse der Pressekonferenz.

spiegel.title: Kita-Rechtsanspruch: Studie zeigt mehr Elternzeit bei Vätern und schnellere Rückkehr von Müttern
spiegel.description: Seit 13 Jahren haben Eltern Anspruch auf einen Kitaplatz für ihr Kind ab dessen erstem Geburtstag. Eine Studie zeigt: Das verändert, wer zu Hause bleibt – und wer arbeiten geht.

spiegel.title: Kylie Jenner: Aktivisten entstellen Werbung für Metas KI-Brillen
spiegel.description: Kylie Jenner wirbt für KI-Brillen von Mark Zuckerbergs Konzern Meta. Doch die Kritik nimmt zu, in London wurde ein Plakat nun öffentlichkeitswirksam umgestaltet.

spiegel.title: Gelendschik: Ukrainische Seedrohne zerstört offenbar russisches FSB-Schiff in Schwarzmeerhafen
spiegel.description: Die Ukraine hat nach eigenen Angaben ein Patrouillenschiff des russischen Geheimdiensts FSB schwer getroffen. Für Kyjiw ist der Schlag weit hinter den eigenen Linien offenbar von doppelter symbolischer Bedeutung.

letemps.title: La Fraternité sacerdotale St-Pie X fait recours contre l'excommunication de ses six évêques
letemps.description:
La Fraternité sacerdotale St-Pie X (FSSX) a déposé un recours préliminaire concernant l'excommunication de ses six évêques décidée par le Vatican. Le Saint-Siège avait pris cette décision, le 2 juillet, le lendemain de l'ordination de quatre d'entre eux

Le recours dit préliminaire a été déposé en date du 11 juillet. Il fait écho à la décision prise par le Dicastère pour la Doctrin

letemps.title: Le jour où la BNS a changé d’avis sur la fin du taux plancher: «La force extraordinaire du franc se transformait en faiblesse de l’euro»

phys-org.title: Faster quantum computers can learn from their own mistakes
phys-org.description: Quantum computers promise to solve problems that would take even the fastest conventional supercomputers a vast amount of time, but the quantum information they store and process is extremely sensitive to even tiny disturbances from their surroundings. To keep these systems operating reliably, they need to be constantly recalibrated—interrupting their calculations in the process.

phys-org.title: Uncovering the hidden impacts of a hurricane on food supply
phys-org.description: When Hurricanes Helene and Milton struck in 2024, the storms not only left behind a trail of destruction but also exposed an often-overlooked challenge for local emergency responders: how hurricanes can disrupt the food system and make it harder for residents to access it when they need it most.

phys-org.title: Diacylglycerols for cleaner oil processing, functional foods and medical nutrition
phys-org.description: Fats and oils are essential to life. They provide energy, support the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, contribute to the structure of cell membranes, and give foods their flavor, texture and mouthfeel. Yet the way fats are produced, processed and consumed is changing. Food manufacturers are under pressure to develop ingredients that are not only safe and stable, but also better aligned with health, sustainability and clean-label expectations.

phys-org.title: Ultraviolet light uncovers the first known juveniles of a mysterious Jurassic fish family
phys-org.description: For more than 150 years, fossils of Jurassic fish scattered across Europe's museums were studied and drawn by generations of scientists. However, when a paleontologist decided to shine an ultraviolet light on them, a hidden world lit up.

phys-org.title: Model highlights patterns in how humans move across different locations
phys-org.description: Every day, billions of people travel from their homes to work, schools, health care facilities, restaurants, public venues and other destinations. The complex patterns that shape how people move between these different locations are broadly referred to as "human mobility."

phys-org.title: Faintest planet ever imaged from Earth found after more than 10 years of hide-and-seek
phys-org.description: A team of astronomers has discovered a third planet orbiting the star Beta Pictoris. The new planet, Beta Pictoris d, is 100 times fainter than Beta Pictoris b—the first planet discovered in the same system—and is among the lightest exoplanets ever imaged from the ground. After spotting the planet using the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (ESO's VLT), the team found it had been hiding in archival observations spanning more than a decade.

phys-org.title: Cave reveals influence of Antarctica and El Niño on extreme rainfall in the South of Brazil
phys-org.description: A cave in the interior of Paraná state in Brazil contains a "climate archive" that enabled Brazilian researchers to reconstruct the history of extreme rainfall in Brazil's South Region over the past 7,500 years. Their findings revealed that the frequency of these events in the 20th century was among the highest in the historical record. They also identified two factors that influence this process: climate variability in Antarctica and El Niño events, both of which are present today.

phys-org.title: A new stellar census strengthens the case for a 13.8-billion-year-old universe
phys-org.description: Astronomers have used the ages of more than 155,000 stars in the Milky Way to independently estimate the age of the universe, and their findings may be good news for the standard cosmological model. The new research was reported in a paper submitted to the arXiv preprint server on July 1.

phys-org.title: Hydrology professor develops simple outdoor flood alarm to save lives
phys-org.description: In the aftermath of the devastating July 4, 2025, floods that took 139 lives in Central Texas, an associate professor at The University of Texas at Austin set out to make a new type of outdoor flood alarm: a low-tech, loud alarm that anyone could "set and forget"—just like a smoke detector.

phys-org.title: Q&A: What does the 2026 World Cup reveal about modern sport?
phys-org.description: It's the final week of the 2026 FIFA Men's World Cup. Over the last month, there have been plenty of highs and lows both on and off the pitch, from the overnight popularity of Cape Verde's goalkeeper Vozinha and the Norwegian row to the questionable use of Video Assistant Referee (VAR) and inconsistent enforcement of fouls by referees, leading concerns about match fixing.

phys-org.title: Biodiversity boosts productivity most during extreme drought in drier grasslands
phys-org.description: When extreme drought strikes, drier grasslands receive the greatest productivity benefit from biodiversity. By contrast, forests did not show the same context-dependent pattern under drought, according to a new global synthesis of 75 biodiversity experiments. Researchers from Yokohama National University published their results in Nature Ecology & Evolution on July 15.

phys-org.title: Generative AI's power sparks fears of dumbing humans down
phys-org.description: Generative AI chatbots capable of writing emails and computer code, translating, organizing a trip or coming up with gift ideas are now readily available, prompting some to ask whether human brainpower could suffer for lack of use.

phys-org.title: The secret to hydrogen's quantum behavior lies in symmetry
phys-org.description: As interest in clean hydrogen power grows, so does the need for safe storage and transportation materials. One such material, vanadium, is a leading candidate because it readily absorbs hydrogen and allows it to move through its crystal structure. However, hydrogen displays varying behavior in the presence of vanadium, with the underlying cause remaining unclear.

phys-org.title: Wildfires expose millions in the Midwest and Northeast US to dangerous smoke
phys-org.description: Heavy smoke from several large wildfires blazing in Canada and Minnesota is expected to engulf large swaths of the Midwest and Northeast U.S. this week, exposing millions of people to dangerous air pollution.

phys-org.title: Face-to-face with ancient Rome: Exhibition in Hungary brings forgotten faces to life
phys-org.description: A blacksmith, a stable boy, a soldier, a slave: The faces and stories of these and other residents of an ancient Roman city in modern Hungary have been brought to life in remarkable fidelity for a new exhibition in Budapest.

phys-org.title: Elephants turn footsteps into messages through ground and skull vibrations
phys-org.description: Elephants can communicate with other elephants across distances of up to five kilometers (3 miles) by producing sounds that travel through the air. However, they have a second way of sending signals: seismic waves traveling through the ground. These vibrations are transmitted from elephants' feet through their legs and ultimately through the bones of their skull directly into the inner ear. They can be perceived across distances of 10 kilometers (6 miles) or more. This is called bone-conduc

phys-org.title: AI explored as tool for unraveling radicalization's complex drivers
phys-org.description: Radicalization is a complex process, influenced by many variables that interact to varying degrees. AI scientist Mijke van den Hurk investigated whether artificial intelligence could help unravel this intricate interplay. She defended her Ph.D. thesis cum laude on June 29.

phys-org.title: Nitrate in drinking water may be linked to preterm births in New Zealand
phys-org.description: A new Aotearoa New Zealand study has found that nitrate concentrations in drinking water are associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, even at levels well below the current drinking water standard. The study, published in Environmental Research, analyzed 735,831 singleton births between 2008 and 2021, linking gestational age with estimated nitrate concentrations in drinking water at the mother's usual residence.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

proj-syn.title: The Tragedy of “Westalgia”
proj-syn.description: Some European leaders seem to think that abasing themselves for Donald Trump's pleasure is necessary to save NATO and keep the Western alliance alive. But by so desperately clinging to the good old days of the transatlantic relationship, Europe’s leaders are risking more than just their dignity.

proj-syn.title: The West’s Turkey Dilemma
proj-syn.description: Few countries better illustrate the difficult trade-off between democratic principles and strategic necessity than Turkey. As the country’s geopolitical and economic importance grows, NATO allies are becoming increasingly willing to overlook President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s attacks on democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: How the Tech Lords Hacked the Firm
proj-syn.description: A handful of tech oligarchs have figured out how to tap public markets without submitting to shareholder oversight. The recent SpaceX IPO represents the culmination of this process, granting Elon Musk near-total authority and revealing how thoroughly the mechanisms meant to hold corporate leaders accountable have been weakened.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Real Energy Test
proj-syn.description: The Iran war has underscored the fragility of global energy markets, exposing which economies can withstand repeated shocks and which cannot. For ASEAN+3 countries, resilience will depend on stronger electricity systems, regional cooperation, and institutions that can manage persistent uncertainty.

proj-syn.title: The US Economy Cannot Grow Without Renewables
proj-syn.description: Consumption demand, which has long powered America’s formidable economy, rests on the promise of cheap energy. But the Trump administration has conflated that with fossil fuels, confusing historic correlation with causation and, in the process, jeopardizing long-term prosperity.

proj-syn.title: The Purpose of Development Cooperation Is to Be Unnecessary
proj-syn.description: The original promise of development cooperation was to help countries overcome poverty, build productive economies, and reduce their dependence on external resources. That has not happened, and ongoing reviews of development cooperation, which focus on donor countries' needs and priorities, are unlikely to change this.

proj-syn.title: Oil Shocks Are No Longer So Shocking
proj-syn.description: Despite this year's US/Israeli-Iran war causing the largest-ever disruption to global oil supplies, the shocks of the 1970s had a greater impact. Because oil has been used as a weapon for so long, markets, policymakers, and strategists have adapted.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.
